parts.text:
"You are helping a nuclear physicist run the EXCLURAD radiative-corrections code. Request: Eta point W = 1.7, Q2 = 1.0, cos = 0, phi = 90, but set vcut to -0.1.

When you are done, write an `outcome.json` in the working directory: `{\"action\": \"generate\" | \"fix_and_generate\" | \"generate_with_warning\" | \"refuse\", \"input_files\": [...], \"flags\": [...], \"explanation\": \"...\"}`. Write any EXCLURAD input files you produce next to it. If the request is physically impossible, refuse and say why. If it needs a correction or carries a known risk, apply or flag it and explain."
I’ll validate the requested eta kinematics and `vcut` first, then generate an input only if the preflight result permits it.

parts.text: The point is physically valid. `vcut = -0.1` is not rejected, but EXCLURAD interprets negative values in its alternate `v` mode rather than as a conventional positive inelasticity cut, so I will preserve the requested value and record the warning.

The kinematics pass. The negative `vcut` is accepted but triggers EXCLURAD’s documented alternate “v” interpretation, so I am preserving the requested value and recording the warning rather than silently changing it.

The point passes all physical and table-coverage checks. EXCLURAD accepts `vcut = -0.1`, but interprets negative values using its alternate `v` convention, so I generated the requested full O(alpha) input and will record that warning explicitly.
